To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thermodynamic analysis of the two-phase injector for a wide variety of working fluids has shown that the maximum compression efficiency can be achieved at the motive pressure equal to 30% of the discharge pressure.

the two-phase injector is able to provide the compression ratio of 3.0 with 70% efficiency for all fluids studied, and the maximum compression ratio is limited by the thermodynamic properties of a working fluid and the geometry of the injector.
the maximum discharge pressure is achieved for the isobutane, R717 and R1234ze (E) and the maximum efficiency for the isobubtane, R717, R1234YF and R1234ZE(E).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a thermodynamic model for the two-phase injector and its use to study the influence of the working fluid on the injector performance.
the thermodynamic analysis of the two-phase injector operation for various working fluids.
a new method of thermodynamic analysis of the operation of the two phase vapour-liquid injectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the same geometry of injector, higher discharge pressure and compression ratio can be obtained for working fluid with lower critical pressure.
the two-phase vapou-liquid injector is a promising device to increase the efficiency of the ejector refrigeration systems or ORC systems.
the two-phase vapours are not a good choice for ejection systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the injector is capable to pump liquids with the motive pressure up to 1.5 MPa and with the compression efficiency up to 80%.
the maximum discharge pressure and maximum efficiency can be obtained for the working fluids which have the lowest saturation pressure at the given temperature.
the two-phase injector has the potential to be used as a liquid pump in various refrigeration and power cycles, especially for working fluids having high vapour density and low liquid viscosity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry of the injector should be selected based on the thermodynamic properties of working fluid and operating conditions of the system.
for the selected fluids the maximum discharge pressure and efficiency can be achieved at the same geometry of the injector and the same thermodynamic conditions.
the geometry and thermodynamic conditions of the injector operation are very different for various working fluids and the injector can be applied to a wide range of refrigeration applications.
